title: S&P Global PMI Commodity Price & Supply Indicators (Sep 2026 data) — 11:00 ET, the semiconductor and oil channel as its own series
source: EST: read verbatim off S&P Global's own calendar listing, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, RE-FETCHED DIRECT BY THIS LANE 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes) rather than carried from the proposal: 'October 01 ... 15:00 UTC S&P Global PMI Commodity Price & Supply Indicators'. 15:00 UTC is 11:00 ET under EDT. Corroborated one rung further on the same session's fetches: S&P Global's own press-release index (pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/PressReleases?language=en, HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes) carries a REALIZED release of this exact series — 'September 01 2026 15:00 UTC | S&P Global PMI Commodity Price & Supply Indicators' — and that release's own PDF, fetched direct (HTTP 200, 125,703 bytes), opens 'Embargoed until 1100 EDT (1500 UTC) 1 September 2026'. So the 11:00 ET slot is observed in a shipped release, not inferred from a schedule page alone. The DAY rule is weaker than the manufacturing PMI's and is stated as such: the calendar publishes release rules for only three series ('Manufacturing PMI: first working day', 'Services PMI: third working day', 'Whole Economy PMI: third working day') and this is not one of them; its first-working-day cadence is inferred from the realized 09-01 instance plus its slot-mates, the JPMorgan Global Manufacturing PMI and the Mexico/Colombia manufacturing PMIs, all of which are first-working-day releases. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap, not on date doubt: market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix for a private PMI compiler (ISM: covers ismworld.org, CAL: is 'automated aggregator cross-ref', and this is the publisher's own primary), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Supersedes proposals/sp-global-pmi-commodity-price-supply-2026-10-01.from-sp-global-manufacturing-pmi-2026-10-01.json, which read the same calendar row; the proposal and this fetch agree on date and time.
notes: THE REASON THIS EVENT WAS PROPOSED IS REFUTED BY ITS OWN LAST REALIZED PRINT, AND THE REPLACEMENT REASON IS BETTER. The proposal filed it as the fuel/supply channel of the Iran escalation. The 09-01 release (data collected 12-27 August 2026, one day BEFORE the 08-28 WTI move began) says the opposite in its own words: 'Global price pressures were at their lowest since prior to the war in the Middle East began', 'oil shortages reached their lowest for six months', Global Supply Shortage Index 1.8 -> 1.6. What the release actually carries is a SEMICONDUCTOR signal: semiconductor price pressures at ~22x the long-run average and highest since June 2022, supply shortages >4x, Electrical Items 9.5x, attributed by S&P Global's own economist to 'reported investment in AI-related technologies'. That is the channel this calendar's names sit in. TIMING IS WHY 10-01 MATTERS: the September-data edition is the FIRST whose entire collection window post-dates the escalation (WTI 83.40 on 08-28 -> 94.46 on 09-09, +13.3%; Brent 89.31 -> 99.52), so it is the first print that can reverse a five-month easing trend, and it lands three days before opec-plus-meeting-2026-10-04. TRADEABILITY MEASURED AT NIL, on this event's OWN slot rather than a borrowed one: the 11:00-11:15 ET window on the three inferred release days ranks above its own all-sessions median on 6 of 15 instrument-days (SPY/QQQ/TLT/IWM/^TNX) against a 50% null, and is indistinguishable from its own neighbours (5/15 for 10:45-11:00, 6/15 for 11:15-11:30). NEW METHOD FINDING that sharpens the sibling ledger's: the month-start confound is LOCALISED to the opening hour — the 09:30-10:30 hour ranks above its own median on 10 of 15 release-day instrument-days and at or above p78 on 7 of 15, while the 10:30-11:30 hour ranks above median on only 5 of 15 and at or above p78 on ZERO of 15. Two structural notes: this release's data are NOT REVISED after first publication (unlike the manufacturing final, whose whole story is a revision), and its 15:00 UTC slot is shared with the JPMorgan Global Manufacturing PMI, so the sibling ledger's use of 11:00-11:15 as a 'placebo' window was contaminated — that window is this release's own slot. NOT A TRADE: status is estimate, symbols is empty, no house playbook is macro-keyed. Full ledger: docs/research/events/sp-global-pmi-commodity-price-supply-2026-10-01.md.
